body.statement:
For every \(P\in\mathcal F_s\) and smooth four-density path with tangent \(\delta\), the selected lifted map \(P\mapsto(\widetilde T(\widetilde y_j))_{j=1}^J\) is Frechet differentiable and its derivative is exactly \(\mathcal D_P[\delta]=\mathcal H_P[\delta]+ ig(
abla\mathcal L_B^{-1}\Pi_0[\alpha(e_{C1}-e_{C0})+e_{T0}-e_{T1}]-
abla\mathcal L_B^{-1}\Pi_0[(\mathsf C
abla\alpha)\cdot
abla\mathcal L_{\mathsf C}^{-1}(e_{C1}-e_{C0})] ig)_{\mathcal Y_J}\), where \(\mathcal H_P[\delta]=(\dot a_T-
abla\mathcal L_B^{-1}\Pi_0[(\mathsf C
abla\alpha)\cdot\dot a_p])_{\mathcal Y_J}\), \(\dot a_p=\partial_t a_{p_t}|_{t=0}\), and \(\dot a_T=\partial_t a_{T_t}|_{t=0}\). The coefficient multiplying the pulled-back inner equation satisfies \(B D^{-\mathsf T}=\alpha\mathsf C\). The map \(\delta\mapsto(\dot a_p,\dot a_T)\) has cellwise Riesz scores with uniformly bounded \(L^2(P_g)\) norms. Consequently \(\mathcal H_P\) contributes \(O(1/\log(1/h))\) to \(\Sigma_h(P)\), and its cross-covariance with the Green score is \(O(1/\sqrt{\log(1/h)})\), both uniformly over \(\mathcal F_s\). This strictly extends the one-target density-curve derivative in GonzalezSanzSheng2024Linearization to a four-input nested map with a generated target law and nonzero harmonic translation modes.
body.justification: The identity exposes every generated-target path, separates the bounded harmonic translation mode, and reduces the singular part to one outer elliptic inverse.
body.gap: GonzalezSanzSheng2024Linearization differentiates one target-density curve with a fixed source; it does not differentiate an outer map whose target is itself an estimated pushforward through an inner map.
body.consumer: The exact weights determine which of the four Card--Krueger cells drives uncertainty in each bivariate counterfactual arrow.
body.proof_tex:
Write \(a=f_{C0}\), \(b=f_{C1}\), \(r=f_{T0}\), and \(t=f_{T1}\).  We first dispose of the harmonic component without silently imposing a normalization.  The chain construction in the proof of lem:torus-cic-identification supplies a single-valued torus potential \(u_F\) satisfying dual equality on the graph of every optimal map \(F\).  On the cut-free smooth branch, differentiating that equality in its first coordinate gives
\[
\nabla u_F(x)=\partial_x c_{\mathbb T}(x,F(x))=x-\widetilde F(x),
\]
where the chosen lift difference is the unique shortest displacement.  Thus \(\widetilde F(x)-x=-\nabla u_F(x)\) is the gradient of a periodic function.  Comparing with \(\widetilde F(x)-x=a_F+\nabla\phi_F(x)\) and integrating over the torus gives \(a_F=0\).  Hence \(a_p=a_T=0\) throughout a sufficiently small regular path, so
\[
\dot a_p=\dot a_T=0,
\qquad
\mathcal H_P[\delta]=0.
\tag{1}
\]
This also proves the asserted cellwise Riesz representation: every harmonic score is the zero function and has \(L^2(P_g)\)-norm zero.

Let \(u\) and \(v\) be the mean-zero derivatives of the periodic inner and outer potentials.  Differentiating
\[
b(p(x))\det S(x)=a(x)
\]
and using \(D\det(S)[D^2u]=\operatorname{cof}(S):D^2u\), together with \(\operatorname{div}(\operatorname{cof}S)=0\), which follows by differentiating the two-by-two cofactor entries and commuting mixed derivatives, gives
\[
\delta_{C0}=det(S)\,\delta_{C1}\circ p+operatorname{div}(aS^{-1}\nabla u).
\]
Since \(A=aS^{-1}\), this is
\[
\mathcal L_Au=\det(S)\,\delta_{C1}\circ p-\delta_{C0}.
\tag{2}
\]
Set \(w=u\circ R_0\).  The divergence change-of-variables formula
\[
\det(D)\{\operatorname{div}_x Z\}\circ R_0
=\operatorname{div}_y\{\det(D)D^{-1}Z\circ R_0\}
\]
applied to (2), and \(p\circ R_0=T\), gives
\[
\mathcal L_{\mathsf C}w=e_{C1}-e_{C0},
\qquad
w=\mathcal L_{\mathsf C}^{-1}\Pi_0(e_{C1}-e_{C0}).
\tag{3}
\]
The right side has mean zero because it is the pullback of the difference of two density tangents; the displayed \(\Pi_0\) also makes the inverse well typed.

For a smooth test function \(\zeta\), differentiating the pushforward identity yields
\[
\left.\partial_\epsilon\right|_0\int\zeta\,d(p_\epsilon\#P_{T0,\epsilon})
=\int\zeta(p(x))\delta_{T0}(x)\,dx
\int\nabla\zeta(p(x))\cdot\nabla u(x)r(x)\,dx.
\]
Integration by parts, justified by periodicity, therefore gives
\[
\dot q=p\#\delta_{T0}-\operatorname{div}_z\{q(z)\nabla u(p^{-1}(z))\}.
\tag{4}
\]
Differentiating \(q(T(y))\det H(y)=t(y)\), using (4), and applying the displayed divergence change-of-variables identity once more gives
\[
\mathcal L_Bv=e_{T0}-e_{T1}
-\operatorname{div}\{BD^{-\mathsf T}\nabla w\}.
\tag{5}
\]

It remains to verify the coefficient identity, including every Jacobian.  From \(D=S(R_0)^{-1}H\), symmetry of the two Brenier Jacobians, and \(A=f_{C0}S^{-1}\),
\[
\mathsf C
=f_{C0}(R_0)\det(D)H^{-1}S(R_0)H^{-1}.
\]
Moreover, the two change-of-variables equations imply
\[
t=f_{T0}(R_0)\det(D)=\alpha f_{C0}(R_0)\det(D).
\]
Thus
\[
BD^{-\mathsf T}
=tH^{-1}S(R_0)H^{-1}=\alpha\mathsf C.
\tag{6}
\]
Substituting (3) and (6) into (5), and expanding the divergence, yields
\[
\mathcal L_Bv
=\alpha(e_{C1}-e_{C0})+e_{T0}-e_{T1}
-(\mathsf C\nabla\alpha)\cdot
 \nabla\mathcal L_{\mathsf C}^{-1}\Pi_0(e_{C1}-e_{C0}).
\tag{7}
\]
The mean-zero projection may be inserted before each inverse because gradients annihilate constants.  The derivative of the selected lifted outer map is \(\dot a_T+\nabla v=\nabla v\) by (1).  Evaluating (7) on \(\mathcal Y_J\) proves exactly the formula for \(\mathcal D_P\) and \(\mathcal H_P\) in the statement.  Subtracting (2) and (5) at two nearby density tuples, the identity \(\det(M+E)-\det M=\operatorname{cof}(M):E+\det E\) makes the residual quadratic in the density and map increments.  The normalized uniformly elliptic inverses therefore bound that residual by \(C\lVert\delta\rVert_{C^{s-2}}^2\).  This proves Frechet, rather than merely directional, differentiability.

For completeness, the second term has a bounded score.  Uniform ellipticity makes each gradient Green kernel bounded by \(C d(x,z)^{-1}\).  Its kernel is a convolution of two such kernels against the smooth factor \(\mathsf C\nabla\alpha\), and the elementary split into \(d(x,z)\leq d(x,u)/2\), \(d(z,u)\leq d(x,u)/2\), and the complement gives
\[
\left|\int_{\mathbb T^2}\frac{dz}{d(x,z)d(z,u)}\right|
\leq C\{1+|\log d(x,u)|\}.
\]
The right side is square integrable in dimension two.  Hence the generated-target score has uniformly bounded \(L^2(P_g)\)-norm.  By (1) the harmonic variance and its Green cross-covariance are actually zero, which is stronger than the two asserted orders.  This completes the Frechet calculation and all ancillary conclusions.
